userDirection: Match the existing assets and Hub area so the interface feels like one world.

concepts.name: 02 — Hub Lab Workbench
concepts.prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup; precise refinement of the supplied existing game UI concept. Render a polished landscape 16:9 screenshot of a PC tower-defense GAME interface, not a web page. Image 1 is the old concept to revise. Image 2 is the actual Copilot Hub scene and is the PRIMARY WORLD/RENDER STYLE AUTHORITY. Image 3 is the actual central Lab building and is the PRIMARY ARCHITECTURE/MATERIAL AUTHORITY. Image 4 is the actual orange Developer Tower and is the EXACT CHARACTER AUTHORITY. Image 5 is the existing campus noticeboard and is a supporting construction/palette reference. User's correction: concepts 2 and 3 must look like one continuous world with these existing game assets and Hub. The old concept's excess ornamentation is NOT authoritative.
Match the existing orthographic Three.js low-poly asset look: simple chunky silhouettes, deliberate faceted planes, small plain bevels, flat solid matte colors, cool ivory concrete/slabs, blue-gray frames, muted cyan opaque glazing, subdued mint grass and faceted teal trees. Soft neutral directional daylight with simple contact shadows like the Hub. Controlled color, no photorealistic PBR, dramatic bloom, brushed-metal textures, paper grain, realistic reflections, cinematic depth of field, golden-hour light, ornate cut corners, fantasy scrolls, luxury leather or massive glowing technology panels. It should look buildable out of THIS project's simple geometry and palette.
Use the real existing Developer as a hovering head only: orange broad angular swept spikes, dark goggles with cyan lenses, dark face with two vertical bright cyan eyes, cream hexagonal ear pods with the curly-brace glyph. No arms, legs, torso or new accessories; no redesign. Keep the model silhouette and colors close to image 4. Other existing portrait identities from image 1 may be reused. No new Tower models: missing portraits are simple dark silhouettes.
Keep functioning game interaction cues: clearly visible rotatable/tiltable 3D model, small orbit arrows, reset icon, small hint "Drag to rotate · Tilt · Zoom". Include seven roster choices named exactly "Base", "Developer", "Tester", "Analyst", "Security", "Architect", "Linter" with Developer selected by a thin mint accent, not huge glowing borders. Simple animation controls named "Rest", "Idle", "Work", "Move", "Place", "Hit", "Resolve"; Idle selected; play/pause, thin time scrub and "1×". Exact stats with restrained graphic meters: "Damage 7 / action", "Work 5 / action", "Speed 2.5 / sec", "Range 5 units". Tiny cost text "Persona +20 Compute" and "Base 30 · Total 50". Label "Playtest stats". Subtle range circle around preview base, no particle cloud. Clear "Back to Hub" button. Header wordmark "COPILOT" with small "TOWER DEFENSE", location "COPILOT HUB", same restrained sans-serif hierarchy as actual Hub, never Glacier. Selected name "DEVELOPER" with role "Direct-output specialist". No invented slogans, quotes, motivational writing, fake stats, decorations with text, buy/deploy buttons or monetization. No website sidebar or data table. The user's assets and Hub must feel like ONE consistent game world. Text crisp, exact, very readable, no perspective-distorted tiny labels. Preserve interaction intent while materially refining the art direction.
REFINE CONCEPT 2 — HUB LAB WORKBENCH. Reframe image 1 into a close ORTHOGRAPHIC ISOMETRIC DOLLHOUSE CUTAWAY of the actual central Lab from image 3. This is the same small building in the Hub, viewed from a slightly closer version of the campus camera, not a separate photorealistic cozy room. The roof is lifted away/cut away to expose one compact inspection bay; retain recognizable white roof-slab edges, blue-gray square pillars, broad cyan window bands, front entrance step and the Lab's simple rectangular footprint. Visible strips of the real paved campus paths, teal trees and a solar-panel corner around the lower building ground it in its original tile. Show the dark blue digital space outside this one small campus excerpt, not an invented sky, city or huge atrium. Do not put a duplicate central Lab in the window view.
The inspection bench is simple off-white slab geometry on a blue-gray base, constructed like the actual Lab; no wood, books, mugs, signs, houseplants, gold trim or cozy cafe props. A small, opaque Developer floats above a compact flat hexagonal test plate on the bench; the selected model is the focal point, taking about one quarter of the screen height, easy to rotate. A blue-gray console at the bench's right holds the four short readable stat meters on a simple dark navy screen, with minimal off-white border. The bench's front apron holds a quiet animation transport strip. Seven squared portrait tiles sit in a physical shallow selection rail along the lower foreground, like campus components, NOT coins or fancy circular medals. Main view has generous empty space. Keep scene isometric, but critical UI labels and animation text clean and screen-aligned for operation. Top overlay header and Back to Hub borrow the thin borders, modest corner radius and mint/white type from the current Hub HUD. Avoid a giant floating black dossier dominating the room. The actual room/table and the existing Developer are the primary experience. One cohesive game screenshot, no inset panels or concept annotations.

REFINE CONCEPT 3 — HUB TOWER CODEX. Keep the selected-dossier and collectible-card interaction from image 1, but reconstruct it as a physical compact catalog station that belongs beside the lab's blue windows, using the campus noticeboard in image 5 as its construction language. A dark blue rectangular frame, flat off-white cap, muted teal header band, pale tan backing ONLY where cards are pinned; clean flat colors. Absolutely remove the massive armored chamfered cream sci-fi panel, orange corner armor, decorative handwritten slogans and shiny trading-card effects of the previous concept.
Camera mostly front/three-quarter with slight orthographic depth. The catalog station is integrated with a simple off-white work counter inside the same Lab architectural style, not floating unattached as a browser page. Through the blue-gray window frames or at the scene margins, retain a legible modest view of the current Hub's flat paths, teal low-poly trees and dark digital grid. Same neutral daylight and flat low-poly render as the actual campus, no cinematic blur. The full station remains clearly in that world.
At left a tidy fan/rack of compact flat portrait dossiers on the noticeboard backing, seven entries in a restrained two-column staggered arrangement, obvious selected Developer; cream squared cards with tiny teal top tabs, minimal depth and simple labels. This is a physical collection of cards, not a navigation sidebar. To the right the selected dossier unfolds across ONE broad, relatively thin off-white display surface built like a campus slab. Developer's exact 3D model hovers over a small squared/hex flat base in the main central preview area. Four precise dark ink/teal stat meters are printed on a small dark navy inset to its right, not a stack of separate rounded web cards. Developer label medium-size, no giant uppercase headline filling the screen. Along the base of the same station sits the simple animation strip with text tabs and transport/scrub controls, without invented animation thumbnail poses. Use the exact actual Hub HUD above with understated 'Tower Codex' subheading. Composition should feel like an accessible game collection screen made from campus architecture, pins and panels. Keep enough screen-aligned readable interface to use comfortably. Single cohesive screenshot, no explanatory inset or concept-sheet annotations.
